headline: Loans and deposits grow, but profit and margin slip
summary_short: M&T's Q3 2026 net income was $775M and diluted EPS $5.04, down from $5.32 in Q2 and up from $4.82 a year ago; net interest margin eased to 3.65%.
summary_long: Taxable-equivalent net interest income was flat q/q at $1.81B as an extra day was offset by lower interest on nonaccrual loans. Average loans grew $2.6B, led by commercial real estate. Noninterest expense rose to $1.39B on data processing, professional services and personnel costs, and the provision rose to $135M. Net charge-offs were 0.35% of loans. M&T repurchased 1.3M shares for $323M; CET1 was an estimated 10.16%. Net operating EPS was $5.08.
confidence_notes: CET1 at September 30, 2026 is estimated by the company. Q/q changes for net income, EPS and ratios are computed from the release's three-quarter table. Net operating EPS excludes intangible amortization and merger costs.

drivers.explanation: Up 2% y/y on lower rates paid on deposits and growth in average loans and securities, partly offset by lower loan yields.
Noninterest expense rose on higher outside data processing and software, professional services, and personnel costs from an extra working day.
Higher residential mortgage banking revenue was offset by lower capital markets and advisory revenue and a lower Bayview Lending Group distribution.
CFO cited strong loan and deposit growth, stable credit and a solid capital position.
